steps.title: Find the client's Fact Find Transcript PDF and let the program read the name and email
do: Find the client's `Fact Find Transcript - DD.MM.YY - (First Surname).pdf` in the client's `2. Fact Find` folder. Try the routes IN THIS ORDER and record EVERY try, failures too:
1  device: the computer (local drive / OneDrive)    2  m365: the Microsoft 365 connector    3  zapier: the Zapier Office 365 tools
Record each try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --route device|m365|zapier --result failed|found --note "what you did"
Bring a copy into the run folder: python3 {scripts}/run.py source {run} --file <local copy of the PDF> --route <the route>
Then: python3 {scripts}/run.py client {run}

The program reads the client's name and personal email from the Fact Find. If it has no usable email, ask Paul for it and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py client {run} --email ADDRESS --said "Paul's own words". Never invent or guess an address.
steps.proof: the PDF was read by the program, it is for the client Paul named, and a usable email is settled

steps.title: Record the facts of the follow-up, each with its source
do: Record: python3 {scripts}/run.py facts {run} --date DD/MM/YYYY --time HH:MM --last-contact DD/MM/YYYY --contact met|spoke --topics "Risk,RA,..." --source "where these came from" [--needs "item; item" --needs-source "where they came from"]
For a RESCHEDULE only the new --date, --time and --source are needed.

The program refuses a date in the past, a follow-up date that is not after the last contact, a topic that is not in the fixed list, and 'what we need from you' items with no source. Never invent an item.
steps.proof: the facts are recorded, valid and sourced

steps.title: The program builds the exact invite and the message to Sitamah
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}
It writes out/invite.json (the exact arguments for the Microsoft 365 tool), out/invite.txt (the same invite in plain words) and out/sitamah.txt. You never type or edit any of them.
steps.proof: the invite follows every rule and is exactly what the program builds from the facts

steps.title: Show Paul the full invite and the message, ask ONE question, record his yes
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py show {run}

Put everything it prints in your reply (the full invite, the message to Sitamah) and ask exactly the one question it gives. This is a REAL SEND: the client is emailed the moment the event is created. Never send before his clear yes.
When he says yes, record his own words: python3 {scripts}/run.py approve {run} --said "his exact words"
If anything about the invite changes, run build and show again: the earlier yes then no longer counts.
steps.proof: Paul's yes is recorded for exactly this invite and message, after he was shown them

steps.title: Send the invite with the Microsoft 365 tool, then tell Sitamah once
do: Follow the rules below. Then record what the tool RETURNED (copy the values it shows; do not retype them from the invite):
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} event.id <the id>        event.subject <...>      event.start <...>      event.end <...>
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} event.attendee <the client's email>      event.online yes   (new invite only)
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} sitamah.sent <the message id or sent time>
For a reschedule record event.id, event.start, event.end and sitamah.sent.
steps.proof: what the tool returned equals the approved invite, and the Sitamah message is recorded as sent

steps.title: Log the meeting on the board's Fact Find card, as today
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py log {run}
Log the lines it prints on the client's Fact Find card under Actions Taken (the board's card, as today), then record: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} log.done yes

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final
Put the short audit it prints in your reply exactly as it is: one line per check with a green tick or a red cross, one closing line for what is only attested. Nothing longer.
Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
